topic: Classifying plants and animals by habitat
key_concepts: Living organisms need food, water, air, sunlight, and shelter to survive.
A habitat is the physical space where an organism lives.
An organism can live only in a habitat where its basic needs are met.
Habitats provide sunlight, air, water, food, and suitable temperature.
Plants and animals can be classified as terrestrial, aquatic, or aerial based on habitat.
Terrestrial habitats include forests, grasslands, deserts, and mountains.
Aquatic habitats include oceans, rivers, lakes, and ponds.
Aquatic habitats are divided into freshwater and marine habitats.
Freshwater habitats include rivers, lakes, wetlands, and springs/oases.
Marine habitats include oceans, coral reefs, estuaries, open ocean, and intertidal zones.
Oceans are large saltwater bodies while rivers are flowing freshwater bodies.
Organisms have adaptations that help them survive in their habitat.
